newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol shares slide after results.
newsitem.headline: Sasol shares slide after results.

text.p: Synthetic fuel and chemical producer Sasol Ltd's shares fell on Tuesday on year results which came in below market expectations, dealers said.
"The most conservative estimates were for an earnings per share of 237. So they came in well below expectations," one dealer said.
The company posted earnings per share of 207.7 cents for the year to December 25 1996 from 174.1 cents previously. The dividend was at 65.0 cents from 53.0 cents.
Sasol was the second most actively traded share on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and was down 250 cents, or 4.63 percent, to 51.50 rand at 1345 GMT.
Volume was heavy with some 1.1 million shares worth over 60 million rand changing hands in 250 deals.
Dealers said the share touched an intraday high of 54.50 rand before the results.
"There is a lot of talk on the results. Some are saying they are not as bad, some saying they are. But obviously the market does not like them so much," a trader said.
Sasol Ltd said on Tuesday it expected profit in the second half of its financial year to be similar to that of the first, barring major fluctuations in the rand and international prices.
